question: Who was the Chairperson of the Planning Commission when it was formed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Planning Commission of India** was established on **15 March 1950**, by a resolution of the Government of India, with the aim of promoting a rapid increase in economic development and improvement in the standard of living of citizens.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first Prime Minister of India, was appointed as the **Chairperson of the Planning Commission** at its inception.
 
• The Planning Commission was tasked with formulating **Five-Year Plans** to address India's developmental needs, focusing on economic growth, social justice, and modernization.
 
• The Commission played a key role in resource allocation, policy formulation, and ensuring the coordinated development of various sectors in the country.
 
• Being the Prime Minister, Nehru's leadership and vision were instrumental in shaping the Commission's strategies and goals, emphasizing self-reliance and planned economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• The Planning Commission was established as a non-constitutional and non-statutory body, meaning it was not created by the Constitution of India or any statute.
 
• The primary objective of the Planning Commission was to assess available resources and determine the best strategies for their effective utilization in building the nation.
 
• The Commission was responsible for creating India's **Five-Year Plans**, inspired by the Soviet model of centralized economic planning.
 
• It focused on sectors such as **agriculture, industry, education, health, and infrastructure** to achieve balanced economic growth and reduce disparities.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru served as India's first Prime Minister from **15 August 1947 to 27 May 1964**.
 
• He emphasized **scientific temper, industrialization, and self-reliance** in India's development strategies, which influenced the Planning Commission's policies.
 
• Under Nehru's leadership, the Planning Commission formulated the **First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)**, focusing on agriculture and irrigation.
 
• He was a proponent of socialism and believed in state-led economic planning for equitable development.
 
 
 
• **Replacement of the Planning Commission:**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** on **1 January 2015**, under the leadership of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, to better address the needs of a changing economy.
 
• NITI Aayog emphasizes **decentralized planning** and incorporates state governments as stakeholders in policy formulation.
 
• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog focuses on **policy think-tank functions** rather than resource allocation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan:**

 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and community development** as its primary goals.
 
• The plan was influenced by the **Harrod-Domar growth model**, which emphasized boosting investment for economic growth.
 
• The total outlay of the plan was Rs. **2069 crore**, and it achieved a growth rate of 3.6%, exceeding its target of 2.1%.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) focused on **industrialization** and was influenced by the **Soviet model**.
 
• It emphasized the development of heavy industries and technological advancements to achieve economic self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Planning Commission:**
 
 
• The Planning Commission played a crucial role in India's early economic development and laid the foundation for future policies.
 
• Its emphasis on planned development and resource allocation shaped India's growth trajectory in the post-independence era.
